title: Fish sandwich, fried, on wheat bun, with cheese

content.title: About
content.content: The fish sandwich, fried, on a wheat bun, with cheese, consists of a breaded piece of fish that is deep‑fried until golden, placed between a split wheat bun and topped with melted cheese. It is often served with tartar sauce, fresh vegetables, and fries.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first fish sandwich appeared in the United States in the early 1920s as a lighter alternative to meat burgers.
A crisp coating is achieved by dipping the fish in a batter of flour, eggs, and spices before frying.
Wheat buns give the sandwich a soft texture and a subtle nutty flavor.
Melted cheese is usually a processed slice because it melts evenly and forms a smooth layer.
Some regional recipes add curry or paprika to the batter for extra zest.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Fish, especially marine varieties, provides EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: One sandwich delivers about 20 g of high‑quality protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Contains vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D in fish aids calcium absorption and boosts the immune system.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Melted cheese adds calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Fiber from the bun
items.content: The wheat bun provides a modest amount of dietary fiber that helps digestion.

items.title: Fish or dairy allergy
items.content: People allergic to fish or dairy proteins may experience reactions when eating this sandwich.

items.title: High in fats and calories
items.content: Frying and cheese increase the calorie count; portion control is advised for weight management.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salt in the batter and sauces can raise sodium intake, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Possible contaminants in fish
items.content: Certain fish species may contain mercury; choose reputable suppliers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sandwich hot, right after frying, so the cheese is fully melted. Add fresh lettuce, tomato slices, cucumber, or pickled onions for extra crunch. For a lighter version, use baked fish instead of fried.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The sandwich is best enjoyed immediately. If needed, wrap it tightly in plastic film and refrigerate for up to 24 hours. Store fried fish separately in an airtight container, and keep the bun in a dry place to prevent it from becoming soggy.
